data.turoyo: B mədde d fəlge d-saʕaye aṭ ṭarfayḏan xamidi. Ḥəllan: i kurfayḏan kmayiṯo, yaqiḏo.
data.translation: Im Lauf einer halben Stunde erloschen unsere Blätter. Wir schauten: unsere Schlange war tot, verbrannt.

rationale: Thin I Preterit Intransitive cell; plural burning-fuel subject and explicit elapsed duration.

summary: 92/48 adds plural Preterit Intransitive xamidi with fuel as subject and an elapsed half-hour. The following burnt snake is a separate participant, not the subject of xamidi.
Hors 3/33 is the inherited RT 33 quotation. xaməd refers to masculine ʕAlo, not feminine i nuro; it describes charring and death, with no necessary additional collapse assertion.
Neither occurrence has Detransitive morphology. Keep I Preterit Intransitive and the existing distinction from III auslöschen. No new box or sense is needed.
The inherited speaker note about typical fire use and the NE collapse example is preserved in the underlying entry; no further collapse interpretation is inferred for Hors 3/33.
Does xamidi in 92/48 imply complete extinction or dying down to embers? The verse supports cessation of the leaf fire but does not identify the remaining combustion state.
Correct thr to the in the English note.
